title: New Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman could begin rehab assignment this weekend
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: The Red Sox acquired catcher Adley Rutschman from the Orioles in exchange for three prospects and Carlos Narvaez.
Rutschman is recovering from left wrist inflammation and may start a rehab assignment with a minor league team soon.
Rutschman was an All-Star for the Orioles in 2026, slashing .251/.331/.433 with 19 homers in 67 games.

title: 5 must-watch movies & TV shows streaming right now
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender' streams on Paramount+, expanding the story from the original Nickelodeon series.
'You, Me & Tuscany', a romantic comedy starring Halle Bailey and Regé-Jean Page, is available on Peacock.
Season 4 of 'Ted Lasso' featuring a women's soccer team storyline streams on Apple TV.

title: Could Garrett Crochet return to Red Sox in a bullpen role?
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Garrett Crochet, recovering from injuries, may return to the Red Sox bullpen in 2026 instead of starting rotation.
Crochet hasn't pitched for the Red Sox since April due to left shoulder inflammation and lat tightness.
Interim manager Chad Tracy suggests Crochet's return might be in a bullpen role given recovery setbacks.

title: Lost a python? Boston Animal Care and Control might have it.
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: A ball python named 'Tippy' was found near Ellington Street in Dorchester by Boston Animal Care and Control.
Concerned residents reported the snake after seeing it left in a cage at a community garden.
Tippy is in good condition at Roslindale's animal care facility; officials seek owner information.

title: Tommy DeVito bests Drake Maye, and other takeaways from Patriots’ training camp scrimmage
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Team Blue, led by Tommy DeVito, won the Patriots' scrimmage 22-15 against Team White, led by Drake Maye.
DeMario Douglas impressed with six catches and two touchdowns, contributing significantly to Team Blue's victory.
Key players missing on Friday included Will Campbell, Carlton Davis, and Brenden Schooler due to injuries or personal reasons.

title: A closer look at Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers, offers 11 miles of tidal shoreline.
The town features seven villages, over 20 beaches, and diverse cultural and recreational activities.
Local highlights include The Port Restaurant's oyster specials, Cape Cod Lavender Farm, and Brax Landing.

title: DA’s office says prosecutor’s ‘hot mic’ moment in Lindsay Clancy trial was misheard
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Plymouth DA's office clarified prosecutors said 'shut it off' regarding autopsy photos in Lindsay Clancy's trial.
Defense attorney accused prosecutors of saying 'shut her up' during a 'hot mic' incident as Clancy sobbed.
Judge William Sullivan warned against inappropriate comments, stating violators will be immediately removed from the courtroom.

title: Little boy dancing to DJ on Boston Common has hundreds of thousands of new fans
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A video of 4-year-old Chukwuemeka Ikesinachi-Nwogwugwu dancing on Boston Common went viral, amassing over 200,000 likes.
The boy's mother, Chidimma Ikesinachi, shared the video, highlighting the joy it brought to viewers and their positive reactions.
DJ Miss S. Peace's popup event aims to promote human connection, with encouragement from attendee Kelly Werme sparking Chukwuemeka's dance.

title: Boston wine bar will keep its signature pours, just without the wine
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boston's Licensing Board suspended Barcelona Wine Bar's liquor license for three days due to serving alcohol to underage patrons.
Barcelona Wine Bar will continue its traditional porrón experience using juice and soda, avoiding alcohol during the suspension.
The restaurant implemented stricter ID scanning policies and ordered more scanners to prevent further underage drinking incidents.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Suffolk DA candidates Kevin Hayden, Rachael Rollins, and Linda Champion clashed over ethics and leadership at Roxbury debate.
Hayden and Rollins acknowledged past ethics controversies, with Champion positioning herself as a responsible alternative.
Candidates discussed transparency in police misconduct investigations, with differing views on releasing body-camera footage policies.
